messages:
sarah: Heads-up team — coordinating a multi-service rollout tonight (23:00 UTC window). This touches orchestration-sidecar, runtime kernel batching, and router schema. Need pin/fallback plan, quick rollback steps, and release-note blurb.

deploy-bot: /deploy orchestration-sidecar v3.3.0 scheduled 2023-11-02T23:00Z. PR: https://git.internal/repo/PR-7890. Canary first, then 25% -> 50% if healthy.

matt: Runtime to roll at the same time: runtime v4.1.1 (includes batching heuristics). Router schema bump to v1.10.0 (minor). Console change is a telemetry flag only per @anya. Any DB or API contract changes?

anya: Console: no DB migrations, API contract unchanged. Telemetry flag flips to new format; we can keep a compat flag. Console build 2.1.0 validated against sidecar v3.3.0. I'll add the compat toggle to the promote checklist.

tim: Canary run in staging overnight: batching + kv eviction looked OK under 100rps. We did observe steady heap growth on 1 of 3 canary pods (~300MB over 40m) — not OOM but concerning. Attaching snippet: `heap growth: +7MB/min on pod-2`

leo: Recommendation: do extended canary (90m) with heap profiling enabled before promoting. Keep router pinned to v1.9.9 as a quick safe fallback. Also keep previous runtime image (v4.0.9) in manifests for fast revert.

sarah: Rollback criteria (actionable):
- 5xx rate > 1.0% for 3 consecutive minutes OR
- p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes OR
- OOM observed on >=1 node during canary/promotion
If any trigger, initiate rollback. Owners: @matt revert router, @tim revert runtime image, @anya flip console compat flag.

matt: Quick revert commands added to runbook:
```
# router rollback
kubectl set image deploy/router router=router:v1.9.9 -n production
kubectl rollout status deploy/router -n production

# runtime rollback
kubectl set image deploy/runtime runtime=runtime:v4.0.9 -n production
kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime -n production
```

deploy-bot: Canary started: orchestration-sidecar v3.3.0 -> traffic 10% to canary cluster. Observability hooks: /monitoring create alert temp-orch-canary-errors, trace sample rate +5%.

tim: Canary @15m: error rate stable, latency within 10% of baseline, but heap growth persists on same pod. CPU +3%. No OOMs yet.

leo: Hold promotion. We'll extend canary to 90m, enable heap profile (jmap/jfr) on the affected pod, and run a simulated load spike (50rps for 10m) to validate. If heap growth <50MB over remaining window and no p95 regression, proceed.

anya: I'll draft release notes with a callout to the telemetry flag and add the console compatibility revert steps. Release notes PR: https://git.internal/repo/PR-7890/notes.

sarah: Promotion criteria to production after canary: stable for 90m, 5xx < 0.5%, p95 <= 1.2x baseline, mem growth <=50MB on any pod. If satisfied, staged ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 20m windows with health checks at each step.

matt: I'll coordinate router pin/unpin and add a small schema-compat test to the runbook. Also will prepare a fast rollback job that can be executed by oncall in <5 minutes.

leo: Oncall notice: @oncall-eng please be ready at 22:30 UTC for final preflight. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/release-orch-sidecar. Postmortem owner if rollback: matt.

deploy-bot: Canary extended to 90m per request. Heap profiling toggled on canary pod-2. Trace rate bumped.

tim: Profiling started — will capture traces and upload to /artifacts/heap-profiles/1700001234. If growth continues after profile, we'll trigger rollback.

anya: Standby for console flag toggle at promote step. I'll keep the compat flag on during canary and have the UI team ready to flip.

sarah: Thanks — we'll reconvene at 22:45 UTC for go/no-go. Final checklist: runbook link, revert cmds in place, release notes updated, canary extended, profilers on.

matt: Affirmative. I'll post the quick-exec snippet in the runbook channel as soon as it's pushed.

leo: Copy that. No promotion until heap traces are reviewed.

sarah: Closing loop: if all good after extended canary, follow staged ramp and monitor the alerts. If any rollback criterion hits, follow the rollback steps and notify #incidents.
